candidates.title: The keys to the Internet change on October 11. Are you ready?
candidates.summary: On October 11, 2026, the DNS root switches to a new key-signing key (KSK-2024). Learn what this means for you, and how RFC 8509 trust anchor sentinels allow you to test whether your DNS resolver is ready for the rollover.

reasons: AI-assisted promotion proposal, pending human PR merge approval
2026-10-11 DNS root KSK-2024 rollover; ICANN recommends verifying DNSSEC validating resolvers' trust anchor (key tag 38696). Urgent, operationally actionable.

candidates.title: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
candidates.summary: Prepare for post-quantum authentication by testing certificate ecosystems now. Learn how Microsoft’s PQC TLS Pilot Program helps advance future readiness. The post Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

reasons: AI-assisted promotion proposal, pending human PR merge approval
Microsoft PQC TLS pilot (non-production) raises enterprise PKI, trust-anchor, certificate chain, HSM, and application-interoperability readiness questions distinct from PIV and key generation.
